Conditional matching-scale independence for RG-compatible maps and supplied flows
Two-flavor QED electron-muon threshold running in the decoupling-subtraction scheme
A numerical one-loop SMEFT anomalous-dimension matrix
canonical.reason: The A3 design requires the exact basis, flavor assumptions, regulator, subtraction convention and computed matrix entries; this batch has no such calculation or source-verified matrix input.

sources.title: Aneesh V. Manohar, Introduction to Effective Field Theories (full Les Houches lecture notes)
sources.locator: Full 94-page PDF inspected. Chapter 5 §§5.5–5.7, printed pp. 38–41, equations (5.23)–(5.31); §5.10, printed pp. 46–48, equations (5.49)–(5.60); Chapter 7 §§7.1–7.2, printed pp. 58–60, equations (7.1)–(7.8).
sources.actual_read_extent: The full PDF was opened and the complete relevant matching, RG-evolution, operator-mixing, and one-loop QED threshold passages were read in the browser.
sources.limitations: These passages give particular perturbative EFT/QED calculations. They do not prove the local compatibility theorem, provide a general coupled SMEFT beta matrix, or establish a continuum interacting theory.

contents.name: Full-theory and EFT matching contribution with common infrared dependence

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete matching derivation in §5.5, including the difference of renormalized full/EFT integrals and the separation of matching and infrared logarithms.
source_review.supports: Matching is defined by comparing renormalized high- and low-energy quantities after common infrared terms are separated; the matching scale is distinct from the scales retained in the EFT calculation.
source_review.limitations: The worked integral is a specific perturbative model. It supplies no universal matching coefficient or local scale-independence proof.

contents.name: Split of large logarithms between matching and EFT evolution

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete §5.6 discussion of the UV/IR logarithm split and the scale choices for matching and EFT evolution.
source_review.supports: Choosing a matching scale near the heavy scale and then evolving the EFT separates the large logarithm into matching and running pieces.
source_review.limitations: This discussion motivates a consistency relation but does not prove the general finite-dimensional theorem authored in this batch.

contents.name: IR-expanded matching procedure and cancellation of common nonanalytic terms

source_review.read_extent: Read the full §5.7 argument through the matching-integral conclusion and the stated UV/IR pole cancellation.
source_review.supports: A matching calculation must use compatible full/EFT infrared data; the source explains a method for isolating the analytic hard-scale contribution.
source_review.limitations: The argument is for the displayed perturbative setup and does not assert generic EFT existence or a universal remainder estimate.

contents.name: One-loop coefficient evolution and operator-mixing example

source_review.read_extent: Read the coefficient RGE, its single-coefficient solution, and the complete two-operator mixing example.
source_review.supports: Coupled coefficient vectors can run under supplied anomalous-dimension matrices and mix as the renormalization scale changes.
source_review.limitations: The matrices are particular QCD examples; the batch theorem supplies no beta entries and assumes the matching-flow compatibility identity.

contents.name: One-loop QED fermion threshold contribution and mass-dependent decoupling

source_review.read_extent: Read the vacuum-polarization formula, the momentum-subtraction beta contribution below threshold, and the MS comparison.
source_review.supports: The heavy-fermion contribution decouples in the mass-dependent subtraction treatment and does not decouple automatically in mass-independent MS.
source_review.limitations: This is a one-loop single-fermion result; the example's two-flavor DS boundary conditions are taken from Burgess, and no all-orders statement is made.

sources.title: C. P. Burgess, Introduction to Effective Field Theory (full review)
sources.locator: Full 55-page PDF inspected. §§2.2.1–2.2.2, printed pp. 20–22, equations (40)–(41); §4.1.4, printed pp. 43–45, equations (81)–(86).
sources.actual_read_extent: The full review PDF was opened and the complete Wilson-action scale-cancellation passages and complete electron-muon DS threshold section were read in the browser.
sources.limitations: The review gives a source-specific QED example and conceptual EFT arguments. It does not prove a universal matching-scale theorem, a generic coupled beta matrix, or a bound on discarded orders.

contents.name: Wilson action from a declared high/low split
contents.reason: This batch defines supplied finite-order matching data and does not construct a Wilson action or prove that a generic high-mode functional integral exists.

contents.name: Cancellation of the intermediate Wilson scale in physical observables

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete explanation of how explicit coupling-scale dependence cancels the scale dependence of low-energy contributions.
source_review.supports: The physical prediction is unchanged when the arbitrary intermediate scale only partitions a calculation into matching and lower-energy evolution.
source_review.limitations: This is a Wilsonian explanation, not a proof of the particular finite-dimensional RG-compatibility theorem in this batch.

contents.name: Electron-muon QED model and matching at the muon threshold

source_review.read_extent: Read the two-flavor Lagrangian, relation between MS and physical couplings, and the mass-independent running above the threshold.
source_review.supports: It fixes the two charged-fermion model and demonstrates why a single mass-independent beta coefficient does not manifest low-energy decoupling.
source_review.limitations: The MS equations alone are not the DS threshold example; the DS boundary conditions and piecewise running are taken from the following equations (85)–(86).

contents.name: Decoupling-subtraction beta flow, continuous matching and integrated coupling

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete piecewise DS beta equation, its continuity and low-energy boundary conditions, and the integrated formulas on both sides of the muon threshold.
source_review.supports: The example's source-reported beta data, boundary values, and continuous electron-muon threshold matching.
source_review.limitations: These formulas are a one-loop perturbative QED result and do not report measured values or establish an all-orders decoupling theorem.
